summary: CBS Sports' Brent Brookhouse previews the UFC 295 main card at Madison Square Garden, which lost its planned Jon Jones vs. Stipe Miocic heavyweight title bout when Jones was injured. He gives a best bet with odds for each of five fights, including Prochazka vs. Pereira for the vacant light heavyweight title and Pavlovich vs. Aspinall for the interim heavyweight title. His record for the year stands at 28-28 after a 2-2 result at UFC 294.
one_line: CBS Sports gives best bets and odds for each UFC 295 main card fight, headlined by Prochazka vs. Pereira and Pavlovich vs. Aspinall.
key_facts: UFC 295 lost its planned heavyweight title defense of Jon Jones against Stipe Miocic after Jones suffered an injury.
UFC 295 takes place at Madison Square Garden in New York.
The main event is for the vacant light heavyweight title: Jiri Prochazka vs. Alex Pereira, with Pereira a slight -115 favorite.
Prochazka never lost the light heavyweight belt but vacated it due to a shoulder injury; Jamahal Hill won it and was later injured, leaving the title vacant again.
Brookhouse's best-bet record for the year is 28-28 after a 2-2 result at UFC 294.
Best bet for Diego Lopes vs. Pat Sabatini: Sabatini moneyline (-115); both men have 12 submission victories and neither has a submission loss.
Best bet for Matt Frevola vs. Benoit Saint-Denis: under 1.5 rounds (-143); Frevola has two knockout losses, one in seven seconds, and has not seen a second round in his four most recent bouts.
Best bet for Mackenzie Dern vs. Jessica Andrade: Dern to win by submission (+115); Andrade has lost her three most recent fights, all by stoppage, and has four career submission losses.
Best bet for Sergei Pavlovich vs. Tom Aspinall: Aspinall moneyline (-120); only three of Pavlovich's 19 career fights hit the five-minute mark, and he has five wins in under one minute.
The Pavlovich vs. Aspinall interim heavyweight title fight has +500 odds for ending in the first minute, and +165 for going past 1.5 rounds.
Best bet for Prochazka vs. Pereira: over 1.5 rounds (-150); only three of their nine combined UFC fights ended in under 1.5 rounds.
Pereira said that bringing Glover his belt back to the gym would mean a lot to him.
